alex_cs: Heads-up: Nebula reserved pool onboarding is scheduled for Tue. Need an ops dry-run focused on quota, autoscale, and priming. Can we coordinate owners and a minimal runbook? :white_check_mark:

jordan_sre: I can own the autoscale + perf metrics. What are their expected load patterns (steady/burst)?
maria_pm: Nebula expects ~700 RPS steady on search, with spikes to ~2k for <90s. EU-WEST-1, reserved pool B. They want a morning window around 09:30 UTC.
sam_ml: Model: gpt-big-8k with prefix-sensitive caching. We'll want a cold-start vs hot-cache comparison and a short quality regression check after the warmup. Also suggest a quantized variant candidate for cost testing.
jordan_sre: Draft runbook items: 1) set soft quota: concurrency 350, token/s 280k 2) run warmup script to populate KV cache 3) run ramp test to 2k RPS 4) validate autoscale response and node add latency 5) trigger fallback to hosted-model to verify graceful degradation 6) run eval subset for quality pass/fail
alex_cs: Can you drop the k6 ramp snippet we can run from ops bastion? CS may need to trigger if SRE is on-call for other things.
jordan_sre: Sure. Snippet: ```bash
# from eu-west-1 bastion
k6 run --vus 50 --duration 30s script.js \
  --ramp 50:2000:30s --hold 90s --teardown 20s
```
sam_ml: Priming loop (simple curl): `for p in $(cat prime_prefixes.txt); do curl -s -X POST $ENDPOINT -d "${p}" >/dev/null; done` — run twice to ensure KV is populated. Then run 100 eval prompts and compute diff vs baseline. Abort if quality delta > threshold.
eng-sre-bot: [scheduled-test] created job 1712348901/nebula-dryloop in eu-west-1 for Tue 09:30-11:00 UTC.
maria_pm: Confirming stakeholders and sign-off. Ops prefers non-peak but Nebula wants morning. We'll do quick warmup at 09:30, main ramp at 10:00.
jordan_sre: Ownership timeline: 09:30 warmup (sam_ml + alex_cs), 10:00 ramp (jordan_sre + eng-sre), 10:20 fallback test (eng-sre), 10:40 quality eval (sam_ml).
alex_cs: Quota plan: start with conservative caps (concurrency 350, token/sec 280k). If autoscale proves stable, we'll request procurement increase for go-live.
sam_ml: I'll prepare the eval set and the JS harness to run quality checks automatically post-smoke.
jordan_sre: Alerting thresholds: error rate >0.5% or p99 > 400ms triggers rollback to hosted-model and a pause of traffic. We'll add a runbook step for that.
alex_cs: Action items: jordan_sre -> k6 script + runbook (EOD Fri), sam_ml -> priming script + eval set, maria_pm -> stakeholder confirmations, eng-sre-bot -> create scheduled jobs & alert hooks.
eng-sre-bot: [reminder] scheduled test in 2 days: 1712348901/nebula-dryloop.
jordan_sre: Also propose a simulated failover: during soak, flip routing to fallback node group to verify fallback logic and observe metrics. Keep rollback steps handy.
alex_cs: Who will publish the post-test summary to the Nebula team? I can compile notes and include renewal health signal.
sam_ml: I'll post the quality metrics and include any anomalies.
jordan_sre: I'll publish perf dashboards + logs link.
maria_pm: Procurement is aware of base commit; they'll likely ask about increasing concurrency post-go-live, so include the escalation path.
eng-sre-bot: [completed] dryloop job 1712348901/nebula-dryloop executed. Artifacts at /artifacts/1712348901.
jordan_sre: Quick run recap: peak RPS 2050, p95 92ms, p99 185ms, errors 0.12%. Autoscale added nodes 1->5 in ~50s. Fallback flow exercised successfully.
sam_ml: Quality check: eval delta within thresholds, no regressions flagged.
alex_cs: Thanks team. I'll send the handoff doc + onboarding checklist to Nebula and note renewal as healthy. :thumbsup:
